findings.title: Test cleanup uses literal alias "alias" instead of the variable, leaking IDPs across runs
findings.body: Inside the new `testCacheIDPForLogin` (and also the pre-existing `testCacheIDPByOrg` at line 303), the cleanup is registered with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)`. The string `"alias"` is a literal, not the per-iteration variable `alias`. Each cleanup therefore resolves to an IDP lookup of a non-existent alias and ends up being a no-op (or NPE when invoked on the null resource). All 20 IDPs created in the loop (and the 10 in testCacheIDPByOrg) remain in the realm after the test, which will cause `idp-alias-0` creation to fail on a subsequent run and pollutes the realm state used by other tests. The cleanup should reference the iteration's alias (e.g., `final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; ... addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);`).

findings.title: remove() always calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) even when the cached entry is available
findings.body: The new code unconditionally fetches `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` at the top of `remove()` solely so it can pass it to `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. In the `else` branch the cache already holds a `CachedIdentityProvider` whose model could supply the same information, so the DB round-trip is unnecessary on the common (warm cache) path. Reuse the cached model when available, e.g.: if invalid, fetch from DB; otherwise use `cached.getIdentityProvider()` (and still null-check, since the alias may genuinely not exist).

findings.title: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() rebuilds the Predicate on every invocation
findings.body: `getLoginPredicate()` constructs a fresh `Predicate<IdentityProviderModel>` (stream of `LoginFilter.values()`, reduce, several `and()` chains) every time it is called. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` invokes it four times per update, and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` invokes it once per create/remove, so the same chain is reconstructed repeatedly on hot paths. Cache the composed predicate in a `private static final Predicate<IdentityProviderModel> LOGIN_PREDICATE = ...` and have the method simply return that field.

findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() calls getLoginPredicate().test(...) four times per update
findings.body: Both branches of the invalidation guard re-invoke the (already expensive) predicate twice on each of `original` and `updated`, i.e. four predicate evaluations per IDP update. Store the booleans once: `boolean wasLogin = getLoginPredicate().test(original); boolean isLogin = getLoginPredicate().test(updated);` and use those locals in the two `if` conditions.
